title: Mountain Scenery
statementMd:
Little Bolek has found a picture with $*n*$ mountain peaks painted on it. The $*n*$ painted peaks are represented by a non-closed polyline, consisting of $2*n*$ segments. The segments go through $2*n* + 1$ points with coordinates $(1, *y*_{1})$, $(2, *y*_{2})$, $...$, $(2*n* + 1, *y*_{2*n* + 1})$, with the $*i*$-th segment connecting the point $(*i*, *y*_{*i*})$ and the point $(*i* + 1, *y*_{*i* + 1})$. For any even $*i*$ $(2 ≤ *i* ≤ 2*n*)$ the following condition holds: $*y*_{*i* - 1} < *y*_{*i*}$ and $*y*_{*i*} > *y*_{*i* + 1}$.

We shall call a vertex of a polyline with an even $*x*$ coordinate a *mountain peak*.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d3b6d2bc90cda6280dc17f9b20e84d691d149131.png) The figure to the left shows the initial picture, the figure to the right shows what the picture looks like after Bolek's actions. The affected peaks are marked red, $*k*$ = 2.

Bolek fancied a little mischief. He chose exactly $*k*$ mountain peaks, rubbed out the segments that went through those peaks and increased each peak's height by one (that is, he increased the $*y*$ coordinate of the corresponding points). Then he painted the missing segments to get a new picture of mountain peaks. Let us denote the points through which the new polyline passes on Bolek's new picture as $(1, *r*_{1})$, $(2, *r*_{2})$, $...$, $(2*n* + 1, *r*_{2*n* + 1})$.

Given Bolek's final picture, restore the initial one.

## Input

The first line contains two space-separated integers $*n*$ and $*k*$ $(1 ≤ *k* ≤ *n* ≤ 100)$. The next line contains $2*n* + 1$ space-separated integers $*r*_{1}, *r*_{2}, ..., *r*_{2*n* + 1}$ $(0 ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ 100)$ — the $*y*$ coordinates of the polyline vertices on Bolek's picture.

It is guaranteed that we can obtain the given picture after performing the described actions on some picture of mountain peaks.

## Output

Print $2*n* + 1$ integers $*y*_{1}, *y*_{2}, ..., *y*_{2*n* + 1}$ — the $*y*$ coordinates of the vertices of the polyline on the initial picture. If there are multiple answers, output any one of them.
statementZhMd:
小波列克发现了一幅画，画上绘有 $*n*$ 座山峰。这 $*n*$ 座山峰由一条非闭合折线表示，该折线由 $2*n*$ 条线段组成。这些线段经过坐标为 $(1, *y*_{1})$、$(2, *y*_{2})$、$...$、$(2*n* + 1, *y*_{2*n* + 1})$ 的 $2*n* + 1$ 个点，其中第 $*i*$ 条线段连接点 $(*i*, *y*_{*i*})$ 和点 $(*i* + 1, *y*_{*i* + 1})$。对于任意偶数 $*i*$ $(2 ≤ *i* ≤ 2*n*)$，均满足以下条件：$*y*_{*i* - 1} < *y*_{*i*}$ 且 $*y*_{*i*} > *y*_{*i* + 1}$。

我们将横坐标为偶数的折线顶点称为一座山峰。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d3b6d2bc90cda6280dc17f9b20e84d691d149131.png) 左图展示了最初的画，右图展示了波列克操作后的画。受影响的山峰用红色标出，$*k*$ = 2。

波列克突发奇想，决定搞点恶作剧。他恰好选择了 $*k*$ 座山峰，擦掉经过这些山峰的线段，并将每座山峰的高度增加一（即将对应点的 $*y*$ 坐标增加一）。随后，他重新绘制缺失的线段，得到了一幅新的山峰图。设波列克的新画中的折线经过的点为 $(1, *r*_{1})$、$(2, *r*_{2})$、$...$、$(2*n* + 1, *r*_{2*n* + 1})$。

给定波列克最终的画，请还原最初的画。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 $*n*$ 和 $*k*$ $(1 ≤ *k* ≤ *n* ≤ 100)$。下一行包含 $2*n* + 1$ 个用空格分隔的整数 $*r*_{1}, *r*_{2}, ..., *r*_{2*n* + 1}$ $(0 ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ 100)$，表示波列克画中折线顶点的 $*y*$ 坐标。

保证给定的画可以通过对某一幅山峰图执行上述操作得到。

## 输出格式

输出 $2*n* + 1$ 个整数 $*y*_{1}, *y*_{2}, ..., *y*_{2*n* + 1}$，表示最初画中折线顶点的 $*y*$ 坐标。如果有多个答案，输出其中任意一个即可。
